subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — GearShift peak scenario mapping
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@gearshift.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@gearshift.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial intake for peak scenarios

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — we chatted with a couple of teams internally and want to get ahead of sizing for an expected launch window in Q3. We have some rough traffic characteristics attached (token samples + a quick token-per-session distribution), but high-level:

- Primary product: conversational assistant + long-form summarization pipeline
- Expected peak-day concurrency: ~1.8k concurrent sessions (user sessions that result in a model request)
- Typical prompt length: 120–350 tokens (mean ~180)
- Typical response length: 250–1,500 tokens depending on task (summaries longer)
- Burst shape: 12:00–14:00 local window, roughly 60–90 minutes of sustained 2–3x over baseline

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether that burst profile maps to a different GPU packing strategy than steady-state?
2) What additional sample telemetry would you need to produce a quick Dedicated fleet footprint?

I attached gearshift_token_profile.xlsx and a small JSONL sample (gearshift_traffic_samples.jsonl). We’re aiming to have a prelims deck by next Thursday for our execs.

Best,
Oliver
Head of Engineering, GearShift AI

Attachments: gearshift_token_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet), gearshift_traffic_samples.jsonl (sample payloads)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@gearshift.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial intake for peak scenarios

Oliver — thanks for the signal and the samples, those are helpful. Quick clarifying questions so we size conservatively but avoid unnecessary reserve: 

- Is the 1.8k concurrent sessions measured as in-flight model requests (i.e., holding open the model connection during reply generation), or as user sessions with intermittent calls (many short calls per session)?
- For the long-form summarization path: what percent of traffic do you expect to hit the summarization model vs. the chat model? Even a small percentage of very long responses changes GPU residency assumptions.
- Are low-latency SLOs required for the burst window (p50/p90 targets)? Or is this a best-effort batch-with-low-cost tradeoff?

We usually produce two artifacts: (A) a quick capacity footprint (GPU count by SKU, oversubscription guidance, and expected p95 latency ranges) and (B) a burst playbook (autoscale + pre-warm rules) that maps to billing/commit options. To produce (A) we’ll need: 48 hours of fine-grained telemetry (per-request token counts, latency, model invoked), and a small set of end-to-end traces for representative long responses. The JSONL you sent looks good; if you can add a field that marks request type (chat vs. summary) that will speed the analysis.

I’ll loop in Ben to start a prelim sizer; Dev can help validate our model variant assumptions. Are you available for a 30-minute handoff tomorrow?

— Hannah
Director, Pre-Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial intake for peak scenarios

Oliver / team — putting a sketch on the table based on the numbers here and what Hannah asked for. High-level notes (prelim, ballpark):

- If 1.8k concurrent == in-flight requests holding model context, we look at ~40–60 A100-style GPUs (or equivalent Ampere/Blackwell SKUs) with a 1.8–2.5x oversubscription for chat workloads with median short responses. For heavy summarization (median responses > 800 tokens) GPU residency increases and the count climbs ~30%.
- Burst strategy: pre-warm an extra 15–25% of the fleet 20 minutes before expected window + enable short-lived burst nodes (spot/backfill) for any 2–3x spikes. That reduces steady reserved commit.
- Latency SLOs: if you need p95 < 500ms for conversational requests we’ll need lower oversubscription and tighter batching controls; if p95 tolerance is 1.5–2s we can push more aggressive batching.

I attached a quick CSV (redwood_prelim_sizer.csv) with scenario rows so we can iterate. Dev / Karthik — can you validate the assumptions about multi-model routing and KV cache reuse for the summarization path (i.e., whether summaries reuse any prefix cache)?

Next step: Hannah and I can run the sample through our local sizing script and give you a 1-page capacity estimate by EOD tomorrow. Can you confirm the percent-split for summarization vs. chat? Also, is the traffic regionally concentrated in US east or spread globally (to know if multi-region capacity is needed)?

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_prelim_sizer.csv (scenario rows)

Thanks Hannah / Ben — quick answers to your questions: 

- The 1.8k number is measured as simultaneous in-flight model requests during peak minute (we used internal request trackers that mark model call start/end).
- Summarization traffic: roughly 18% of calls on peak days hit the long-form summarization model; those requests skew much longer (median ~1,100 tokens).
- Latency SLO: primary product needs p50 ~200ms and p95 ~900ms for chat; summaries are allowed up to p95 ~3s. We prefer cost efficiency on summaries as long as they finish within the 3s window.
- Region: primarily us-east with small eu-west fallback (about 8% of traffic).

I uploaded a 48-hour telemetry dump and some labeled traces to the Drive link in the thread — the files are the same names Ben referenced. We’re happy to run the sizing script together tomorrow.

Best,
Lina
Product Ops, GearShift AI
